title: Workshop: Dude, what’s your problem? Understanding problem framing to achieve good solutions.
description: All of us want to solve problems, and many of us pursue professional and civic pathways focused on problem-solving, whether that’s politics, engineering, business, or many, many other pursuits. However, we’re often not aware of the crucial step of problem-framing and how it determines the types of potential solutions that might be generated and their eventual success (or failure). In this workshop, participants will identify problems that plague their lives, look at past cases of effective and ineffective problem-framing and problem-solving, and consider how the problems they’ve identified can be framed to achieve different outcomes. The importance of this process will be underscored with applications in government, technology, business, and other fields.

title: Workshop: Think Before You Click: A Look at Image Verification
description: They say a picture can speak a thousand words, if only those words were all true. In this age of misinformation, AI slop and doom scrolling it’s become easier than ever to consume images online that are misleading, mislabeled or completely false. This workshop will review basic image verification techniques by placing the audience in real breaking news scenarios. Participants will experience in real time how easy it is to share a bogus image and learn how to confirm its authenticity before hitting click.

title: Rethinking Classroom Assessment Techniques
description: Whether you teach a large-enrollment lecture, a small seminar, or a fully asynchronous online class, one challenge remains universal: How do you know what your students are learning before high-stakes exams or major assignments? In this workshop, you will explore the latest edition of Classroom Assessment Techniques (CATs), an updated classic that provides a modern framework for designing real-time, low-stakes assessments across all teaching modalities while addressing the opportunities and challenges of today's AI-influenced educational landscape. Participants will examine the different categories of CATs and learn how to select and adapt strategies that align with specific learning outcomes. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to… 1) Identify appropriate Classroom Assessment Techniques that align with specific course learning outcomes. 2) Use the Course Learning Outcomes Inventory (CLOI) to identify essential course knowledge and skills and align them with low-stakes assessments. 3) Develop a plan for a Classroom Assessment Technique that can be used in an upcoming class session.

AFF events are free and open to everyone in the Texas A&M academic community. Participants may choose to attend a few seminars or enough to complete requirements for the AFF Fellow certificate. title: Stop Refereeing Group Projects: A Plug-and-Play Toolkit for Student Self-Managing Teams
description: This workshop explores how to design and facilitate small group projects that empower students to manage their own team dynamics, workflows, and internal conflicts. Moving beyond generic project guidelines, participants will examine evidence-based strategies to help student teams self-diagnose and self-correct using vetted, classroom-ready working style inventories and peer charters. We will address common pain points—such as free-riders, communication breakdowns, and grading friction—by introducing modular, just-in-time tools that can be deployed immediately to course-correct current groups or archived to launch seamless collaboration next semester. Faculty will walk away with access to a pre-organized digital toolkit containing plug-and-play communication templates, workflow matrices, and student-led escalation protocols designed to shift the instructor's role from group referee to strategic consultant. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to… 1) Design student peer charters and escalation/deescalation protocols to reduce instructor conflict management.

By auditing the assignments and activities you already use, we will explore how small, intentional design tweaks can boost student engagement, success, and retention. This foundational overview aligns with institutional goals while connecting you directly to customized CTE consultation support. title: Demystifying Service-Learning: Elevating Workforce Readiness Through Public-Impact Projects
description: True workforce readiness requires more than technical competency—modern employers are actively seeking graduates who can navigate ambiguity, collaborate across differences, and solve complex community challenges. In fact, the AAC&U national employer report (The Agility Imperative) reveals that 76% of employers are more likely to hire graduates with community-based project experience, and 94% view citizenship development and workforce preparation as a single, unified goal. This introductory session explores how service-learning bridges the gap between student career readiness and real-world problem-solving. We will examine how to conceptualize service-learning partnerships that are deeply reciprocal, mutually beneficial, and sustainable for both faculty and community stakeholders. This foundational workshop is designed to pique your interest and shift your perspective. You will leave with a clear roadmap and direct access to CTE consultation support. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to… 1) Identify key components of reciprocal service-learning partnerships that align with workforce readiness.

title: Getting Started with Panopto: Recording, Managing, and Delivering Course Media

This introductory workshop provides an overview of Panopto's core features and demonstrates how instructors can use Panopto within Canvas to support course content delivery. Participants will explore recording options using the desktop application and web recorder, learn how to organize and share videos, and gain a basic understanding of Panopto's built-in editing tools. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to… 1) Identify key Panopto features available for recording, managing, and sharing course media. 2) Demonstrate how to create and publish recordings using the Panopto desktop application and web recorder. 3) Apply basic editing functions to enhance recorded content.

title: Workshop: Doomscrolling, the Algorithm, and You
description: Many of us consume our news through our social media feeds. How do you know where that information originated? How is the algorithm influencing what you're seeing? Is it a conspiracy theory, AI generated, influencer click bait, or is it accurate news? We’re going to learn why it’s important to trace your sources, analyze how the algorithm is influencing our individual feeds, and practice how to look for the origins of what you’re seeing while social media doomscrolling.

In this interactive session you will examine your strengths and weaknesses as they match with the six Aggie Core Values and discover tangible ways to integrate them into daily life for the strategic purpose of enhancing your resilience.

title: Beyond AI Summaries: Collaborative Reading with Perusall
description: As GenAI makes it easier than ever for students to bypass the intellectual work of reading, instructors face new challenges in designing meaningful learning experiences around course texts. This workshop demonstrates how Perusall can turn reading assignments into interactive learning communities where students collaboratively interpret ideas, challenge assumptions, and learn from one another. Participants will explore assignment design strategies and Perusall features that promote deeper engagement, accountability, and authentic learning. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to… 1) Explain how social annotation transforms reading from an individual activity into a collaborative process of discussion, inquiry, and knowledge construction. 2) Identify Perusall assignment features and activity types that promote student engagement, active reading, peer interaction, and deeper understanding of course content. 3) Design a Perusall-based reading activity that encourages meaningful collaboration, supports course learning goals, and extends learning beyond reading through discussion or classroom application.

description: Teaching is not just about delivering content—it’s about connecting authentically with your students. Through guided reflection, short activities, and examples of pedagogical strategies, participants will explore how their knowledge, experiences, and disciplinary perspectives shape the way they teach. The session will also introduce techniques to manage expectations, establish an effective classroom tone, and select teaching approaches that align with their personality and goals as educators.

Participants will examine how structured peer feedback and a live presentation can promote accountability, meaningful engagement, and authentic demonstrations of learning while supporting a variety of instructional approaches to GenAI. title: Workshop: Dude, what’s your problem? Understanding problem framing to achieve good solutions.
description: All of us want to solve problems, and many of us pursue professional and civic pathways focused on problem-solving, whether that’s politics, engineering, business, or many, many other pursuits. However, we’re often not aware of the crucial step of problem-framing and how it determines the types of potential solutions that might be generated and their eventual success (or failure). In this workshop, participants will identify problems that plague their lives, look at past cases of effective and ineffective problem-framing and problem-solving, and consider how the problems they’ve identified can be framed to achieve different outcomes. The importance of this process will be underscored with applications in government, technology, business, and other fields.

title: Workshop: Think Before You Click: A Look at Image Verification
description: They say a picture can speak a thousand words, if only those words were all true. In this age of misinformation, AI slop and doom scrolling it’s become easier than ever to consume images online that are misleading, mislabeled or completely false. This workshop will review basic image verification techniques by placing the audience in real breaking news scenarios. Participants will experience in real time how easy it is to share a bogus image and learn how to confirm its authenticity before hitting click.

title: Providing Students Multiple Pathways to Demonstrate Mastery
description: The design of an assessment can affect how students demonstrate what they know and whether they have equal access to the assessment. By applying the principles of Universal Design for Learning (UDL), instructors can create flexible assessments that reduce barriers; emphasize authentic demonstrations of learning; and maintain rigorous academic expectations. In partnership with Justin Romack, Assistant Director at the Disability Resources Office, this workshop explores how assessment design influences student access and success. It examines common barriers students encounter in traditional assessments and discusses practical strategies for designing assessments that provide multiple pathways for students to demonstrate their learning. Participants will also discover how generative AI can support brainstorming alternative assessment formats, applying UDL principles to assessments, and simplifying assignment language. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to… 1) Identify common barriers in traditional assessment design that may limit student access and opportunities to demonstrate learning. 2) Apply Universal Design for Learning (UDL) principles to design or revise assessments. 3) Identify ways generative AI can assist with creating alternative assessment formats and redesigning assessments.

title: Workshop: Doomscrolling, the Algorithm, and You
description: Many of us consume our news through our social media feeds. How do you know where that information originated? How is the algorithm influencing what you're seeing? Is it a conspiracy theory, AI generated, influencer click bait, or is it accurate news? We’re going to learn why it’s important to trace your sources, analyze how the algorithm is influencing our individual feeds, and practice how to look for the origins of what you’re seeing while social media doomscrolling.

title: Workshop: Aggie Core Values as a Toolkit for Enhancing Your Resilience
description: Respect, excellence, leadership, loyalty, integrity, and selfless service aren't just words on the entrances to the MSC. Together these principles form a shield of protection with the power to protect not just ourselves but others around us. In this interactive session you will examine your strengths and weaknesses as they match with the six Aggie Core Values and discover tangible ways to integrate them into daily life for the strategic purpose of enhancing your resilience.

title: Workshop: When Loyalties Collide: What Does It Mean to Lead in an Era of Conflicting Loyalties?
description: Our loyalties profoundly shape how we interpret events, information, and people, often in ways we don't recognize. Studies consistently show that two people with different loyalties can witness the same situation and reach completely opposite conclusions. This makes it essential for leaders to critically examine their own loyalties: Why are we loyal to certain ideas, people, or groups? Are these loyalties justified? When should we reconsider or even abandon a loyalty? In this workshop we will explore various definitions and theories of loyalty, which will help you to develop practical frameworks for navigating conflicting loyalties and leading with moral clarity.

title: English Language Proficiency Grammar for Speech: Modal Verbs
description: Is it a suggestion or a requirement? Using the incorrect modal verb can hinder successful spoken communication, leading to confusion. Speakers can communicate more effectively when they utilize the appropriate modal verbs (such as should, might, must) to convey obligations and suggestions. In this workshop, attendees will review and practice modal verbs in the context of giving instructions and corrective feedback. An optional assignment for extended practice will be available. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to... 1. Employ modal verbs (such as should and have to) in the feedback process, conveying constructive criticism and suggestions using appropriate modals. 2. Plan and communicate clear and unambiguous instructions using appropriate modal verbs to convey obligations, recommendations, and suggestions effectively.

title: Digital Accessibility Bytes: Accessible PowerPoint Presentations
description: PowerPoint presentations play a central role in teaching, but design choices such as color contrast, reading order, image use, and slide structure can impact how students access and engage with course content. In this 30-minute session, participants will learn practical strategies for creating accessible PowerPoint presentations. We will explore how to use slide layouts, organize content with a logical reading order, write meaningful alternative text for images, select accessible color combinations, and use Microsoft PowerPoint's built-in Accessibility Checker to identify and resolve common accessibility issues. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to… 1) Utilize the built-in Accessibility Checker in PowerPoint to identify and fix common issues. 2) Apply remediation techniques to improve accessibility in PowerPoint presentations.

title: Workshop: Confronting McCarthyism: Evaluating Evidence as a Historian
description: What does it mean to be a “patriotic” American? How do we define “loyalty” to the nation? And who establishes the standards for allegiance in a democratic society? Using the 1950s’ House Un-American Activities Committee proceedings as a framework, this session explores how we can learn from history when evaluating arguments over national identity and patriotism. Participants will assess how information is used to substantiate arguments and explore how historians critically evaluate evidence for authenticity, bias, and authority.

title: Workshop: When Loyalties Collide: What Does It Mean to Lead in an Era of Conflicting Loyalties?
description: Our loyalties profoundly shape how we interpret events, information, and people, often in ways we don't recognize. Studies consistently show that two people with different loyalties can witness the same situation and reach completely opposite conclusions. This makes it essential for leaders to critically examine their own loyalties: Why are we loyal to certain ideas, people, or groups? Are these loyalties justified? When should we reconsider or even abandon a loyalty? In this workshop we will explore various definitions and theories of loyalty, which will help you to develop practical frameworks for navigating conflicting loyalties and leading with moral clarity.

title: Workshop: I didn’t see that coming…
description: Judgements and decisions rely on assumptions, and even hidden principles that can produce unexpected, or undesirable consequences. This interactive session will use Trolly Car problems and other scenarios to improve your ability to reason. You will learn to draw out and test hidden commitments, and unexpected consequences, cultivating the habit of critically engaging with alternative choices before settling upon a decision.

title: Workshop: Overcoming Errors in Reasoning
description: We’re not typically aware of the shortcuts our brains take to efficiently process information. In this interactive session you will examine how our use of mental shortcuts influences how we think and make decisions. You will learn why these biases occur and develop strategies to minimize their impact on your important decisions and everyday interactions.

title: NACADA Webinar: Deconstructing Burnout in Advising: Reframing Solutions from Self-Care to Prevention
description: This session will explore, unpack, and deconstruct burnout through perspectives and experiences of advisors from various geographic and institutional settings. Advising work may be close to our hearts, but there’s a limit to how much space and energy one can give when passion, a student focus, and self-care are inadequate to prevent burnout. Framed by the 12 stages of burnout and the concept of emotional labor, panelists will examine how higher education fosters certain types of burnout that impact advisors and the profession. Participants will be encouraged to consider their spheres of influence as advisors, managers, and colleagues as we seek to interrupt, intervene, and reframe burnout to address its root causes and learn how the profession can support advisors in this era of change. Participants will be able to: - Identify the symptoms and stages of burnout. - Recognize the impact of burnout on advisors and the profession. - Examine ways of preventing or minimizing burnout rather than relying on self-care. - Understand how to create strategies to help prevent burnout.

title: Tech-Free Instructional Strategies for Engagement in the Classroom
description: Technology can be a tool used for engagement, but what happens when the Wi-Fi fails, a classroom tool is not available, or you simply need a different way to engage students? In collaboration with Elizabeth Garza and Dr. Laura Hammons, this workshop presents practical strategies to help faculty with student engagement regardless of available technology. Participants will explore a variety of low-stakes, low-preparation, and technology-free techniques that can serve as reliable alternatives or complements to digital tools. Together, we will discuss how these strategies can be adapted for a range of teaching environments, including large-enrollment courses, laboratory settings, and other instructional contexts. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to… 1) Identify a variety of low-stakes, technology-free instructional strategies that promote student engagement across different classroom settings. 2) Evaluate how the presented instructional strategies can be adapted to different instructional contexts. 3) Develop a plan that incorporates at least one technology-free engagement strategy into an upcoming class session.

title: American English Vowel System (Part 1 of 4)
description: The vowel sounds of American English are challenging to learners of English because there are so many, and because English spelling does not convey the pronunciation predictably. This four-session series of interactive workshops aims to increase attendees' phonological awareness, and as a result, their listening and intelligibility. Through a variety of activities and handouts, attendees will become familiar with each vowel and with resources to practice listening discrimination and pronunciation on their own. Each attendee has the opportunity to get personalized feedback on their own pronunciation. Those who attend Part 1 will automatically be registered for Parts 2-4 at the same time and place the following weeks.

title: Workshop: Doomscrolling, the Algorithm, and You
description: Many of us consume our news through our social media feeds. How do you know where that information originated? How is the algorithm influencing what you're seeing? Is it a conspiracy theory, AI generated, influencer click bait, or is it accurate news? We’re going to learn why it’s important to trace your sources, analyze how the algorithm is influencing our individual feeds, and practice how to look for the origins of what you’re seeing while social media doomscrolling.

title: Workshop: Leading with Integrity: Giving and Receiving Criticism
description: It’s hard to receive criticism without feeling defensive, ashamed, or angry, and it’s hard to give criticism without worrying about damaging your relationships. As a result, we don’t give criticism even when we know that we should, and we don’t learn from criticism that could have helped us grow. For groups, organizations, and leaders who value honesty and accountability, this is a serious problem, but there are steps that we can take to both give and receive criticism with greater ease and effectiveness.

title: GSPDT: Finding Your Teaching Voice: Understanding Strategies to Identify Your Pedagogical Approach
description: Teaching is not just about delivering content—it’s about connecting authentically with your students. This interactive workshop helps graduate students discover and develop their unique teaching voice—the combination of confidence, authenticity, and pedagogical intention that defines effective instructors and supports the development of effective learning environments. Through guided reflection, short activities, and examples of pedagogical strategies, participants will explore how their knowledge, experiences, and disciplinary perspectives shape the way they teach. The session will also introduce techniques to manage expectations, establish an effective classroom tone, and select teaching approaches that align with their personality and goals as educators. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to... 1. Articulate their emerging teaching identity by reflecting on personal values, experiences, and beliefs about learning. 2. Identify pedagogical strategies that align with their authentic style and disciplinary context. 3. Apply techniques to build confidence and classroom presence, including planning, body language, and interaction strategies.

title: Workshop: How to Read Like a Lawyer
description: Learn to approach texts with the precision and insight of a lawyer. This interactive session introduces you to strategies for reading cases, statutes, and arguments critically and effectively, helping you to break down complex language, identify key issues, and sharpen your analytical skills. Whether you’re preparing for law school or simply want to strengthen your critical reading abilities, this session will equip you with practical tools you can use in any field.

We will examine the Canvas built-in accessibility checker, interpret Ally Course Accessibility Reports to identify common accessibility barriers, and apply recommendations to improve digital course content. title: The Higher-Impact Classroom: Elevating Current Practices Without Increasing Workload
description: Every instructor wants their students to deeply engage, retain knowledge, and succeed, yet the term "High-Impact Practices" can feel like an overwhelming mandate that requires a major remodeling of your course. description: This workshop explores how to design and facilitate small group projects that empower students to manage their own team dynamics, workflows, and internal conflicts. title: NACADA Webinar: The Art of Saying No: Navigating Difficult Academic Advising Conversations
description: Difficult conversations are an inevitable part of academic advising, but they often come with a heavy emotional toll. Whether delivering disappointing news about academic policies, discussing a student's poor performance, or addressing issues like academic dismissal, these challenging interactions can lead to burnout and emotional exhaustion. In this webinar, we aim to equip academic advisors with practical tools and strategies to navigate these tough conversations while managing their emotional well-being. Utilizing Compassionate Directness, the SPIKES protocol, and BRIGHT advising approach, we address the art of saying "no." At the end the webinar, we aim for participants to have actionable insights, self-reflection tools, and self-care strategies designed to enhance their ability to handle challenging conversations and create a healthier, more effective advising environment. Participants will be able to: - Identify personal strengths and areas for improvement in handling difficult conversations, based on self-assessment of common advising scenarios. - Demonstrate the ability to apply at least three effective communication strategies for difficult conversations, including techniques for saying no assertively, through worksheet and role-play exercises. - Create a self-care plan that includes strategies to maintain well-being when engaging in difficult conversations and creating a supportive advising environment.

description: Our loyalties profoundly shape how we interpret events, information, and people, often in ways we don't recognize. title: Workshop: Is this Fair and Balanced?
description: How much do you trust the news media? In this interactive session you will learn strategies for sizing up news reports across traditional and social media platforms. title: Workshop: When Loyalties Collide: What Does It Mean to Lead in an Era of Conflicting Loyalties?
description: Our loyalties profoundly shape how we interpret events, information, and people, often in ways we don't recognize. Studies consistently show that two people with different loyalties can witness the same situation and reach completely opposite conclusions. This makes it essential for leaders to critically examine their own loyalties: Why are we loyal to certain ideas, people, or groups? Are these loyalties justified? When should we reconsider or even abandon a loyalty? In this workshop we will explore various definitions and theories of loyalty, which will help you to develop practical frameworks for navigating conflicting loyalties and leading with moral clarity.

title: NACADA Webinar: Expand Your Toolbox: Integrating Academic Advising and Career Coaching
description: As career readiness and professional skill development become top priorities for higher education, the need for an integrated approach to academic advising and career coaching has never been greater. Advisors are increasingly being called upon to support students not just academically, but in preparing them for meaningful careers beyond graduation. By skillfully incorporating career-focused discussions into existing advising practices, advisors can play a key role in a student's academic and professional success. Through this dynamic webinar, participants will learn how to utilize an integrated advising approach to bolster students’ development by facilitating connections between academic requirements and the cultivation of valuable career readiness competencies. Grounded in practical experience and shared examples, this session provides attendees with the strategies, tools, and resources needed to build their confidence and expand their skillsets. Participants Will be Able To: - Identify ways academic advising, across different student populations, can be enhanced by incorporating career-focused discussions into traditional advising interactions, thus leading to students’ professional success and fulfillment. - Explore areas within current practices in which career-focused discussions can be implemented. - Leverage strategies, tools, and resources to confidently integrate career coaching conversations into advising practices - Develop a plan for fostering a holistic, career-integrated advising environment at their institution

title: NACADA Webinar: From Chaos to Clarity: Building Scalable Advising Systems for Large Caseloads
description: Large advising caseloads are an increasing reality across higher education, often creating tension between operational demands and advisor well-being. As practitioner literature and national conversations continue to highlight the connection between high-volume caseloads and advisor burnout, institutions are seeking structured and sustainable solutions. This webinar explores how advising units can intentionally align operational efficiency with practices that protect advisor capacity while maintaining high-quality student support. Drawing on experiences within an advising center serving undergraduate business students at a large public institution, presenters will outline scalable strategies that promote clarity, consistency, and shared responsibility. Participants will examine structured appointment models, including required versus optional advising touchpoints, as well as tiered advising approaches such as individual, group, and walk-in formats. Presenters will also share cross-team support systems designed to address uneven caseload distribution. In addition, the session will explore advising delivery formats that support accessibility and efficiency, with examples drawn from our in-person and email advising models. The webinar will further highlight the role of standardized documentation practices, centralized resource hubs, and clearly defined advising boundaries in reducing redundancy and preventing burnout. Emphasis will be placed on practical frameworks that can be adapted to institutions of varying sizes and resources levels. Participants will leave with actionable strategies for designing advising systems that balance efficiency with advisor well-being in large caseload environments. Participants Will Be Able To: - Assess structural factors within their advising units that contribute to inefficiency or advisor burnout in large caseload environments. - Design structured appointment models that align required advising touchpoints with institutional capacity and student needs. - Apply tiered advising approaches (e.g., individual, group, and walk-in formats) to improve scalability and resource allocation. - Develop cross-team support systems and standardized documentation practices that promote clarity, shared responsibility, and consistency. - Establish sustainable boundaries and operational practices that protect advisor well-being while maintaining high-quality student support.

title: NACADA Webinar: Practical Strategies for Trauma-Informed Advising
description: As advisors, students frequently reveal the traumatic events of their lives to us. Without professional licensure in mental health services, what should advisors do? For students to access resources that will address their mental health needs, they first need to reveal to a trusted person that they need help. For this reason, it is incredibly important for advisors to know how to use trauma-informed practices to create a safe space for all students to ask for help. At the basis of trauma-informed advising is intentionally enacting the 5 principles of trauma-informed care in our advising practice, including safety, trustworthiness, choice, collaboration, and empowerment” “Harris & Fallot, 2001”. All of these principles are relational skills at their core, highlighting the importance of relational advising strategies when working with students who have experienced trauma. While the practice of trauma-informed advising is primarily relational, it is often difficult to know how to practically enact trauma-informed conversational strategies with students during high-stress advising moments. This session is ideal for advisors who desire to deepen their understanding of trauma and its impact on students, while learning powerful conversational techniques to better empathize with students in distress. Participants Will Be Able To: - Identify what trauma is, how it impacts our stress-response system, and signs of a student in distress. - Use conversational techniques such as validation, scaling questions, externalization, and parts language to empathize with students while also maintaining appropriate boundaries. - Enact practical strategies for taking a trauma-informed and person-centered approach in our work as advisors. - Make effective referrals to mental health services.

title: NACADA Webinar: Rethinking Student Centered: Building an Advisor-Centered Culture for Meaningful Stu
description: Higher education practitioners have historically promoted student-centered philosophies and practices. While well-intentioned, focusing solely on student needs does not account for the professionals who are both responsible for and invested in student learning. We intentionally shifted our focus to be advisor-centered: when advisors are respected and valued within a community of care, they will experience a sense of belonging and be deeply engaged in their profession. This culture mitigates burnout and enhances recruitment, resilience, and retention. Valuing advisor development and well-being benefits both the advising community and students. Cultural change requires ongoing systemic and structural transformation, self-reflection, compassion, and intentional leadership. This presentation explores the benefits of an advisor-centered approach and offers strategies for embedding it into practice. Participants will gain actionable insights to create a sustainable, engaged, and impactful advising community within their organizations. Participants Will Be Able To: - Appreciate the importance of a work culture. - Learn why a culture of support is critical. - Understand the many ways in which culture can be fostered, and that it is difficult, takes time, and is ultimately extraordinarily rewarding. - Reflect upon the kind of a work culture participants might want to foster in their own work environments, given the personalities of the leadership and staff.

title: NACADA Webinar: Empowering the Mid-Level: Creating Sustainable Professional Pathways
description: Academic advising professionals are often celebrated for their commitment, longevity, and deep institutional knowledge. While some advisors aspire to senior leadership roles, others find fulfillment in remaining “helping professionals” focused on direct student support. When traditional promotional pathways are limited or unavailable, feelings of stagnation and diminished recognition can emerge. This webinar will reframe career advancement by exploring the value of horizontal and lateral career movement as intentional strategies for professional development through the lens of (a) advising administrators, (b) professional advisors, and (c) faculty advisors. Participants will engage in a reflective, practical career-success planning aimed at redefining growth beyond the conventional “climbing the ladder” model. Explore meaningful ways to build a rich, rewarding career that aligns with personal values, institutional needs, and long-term sustainability. Participants Will Be Able To: - Understand the complexity of being an advising middle manager. - Understand the intersection between advising models and institutional management structures. - Discuss the history and development of mid-career practitioners within academic advising and other niches of higher education. - Develop strategies to overcome professional challenges. - Gain insights on sustainable approaches to keep current and future advising practitioners within the field.

title: NACADA Webinar: Advising Undecided Reimagined: Framework, Praxis, and Storytelling for Exploring Stu
description: In 2023 the First Year Advising Center and Career and Life Design at Oakland University were tasked with coming up with a strategy to better support and retain our Undecided (Exploring) student population. Our division leadership created an initiative to develop better lines of communication between departments and to model effective collaboration in a common goal of retaining and supporting this unique student population. Early on our goal was to define the overarching reason we did not retain our Exploring student population at the same rate as their peers. In the years following the initial pilot program we developed resources, strengthened campus partnerships, and best practices for academic advisers and career coaches. These resources have evolved over time and we are excited to share what has proven to be most effective. This session will provide a brief overview of how we built the foundation of our program along with highlighting strategies our colleagues across campus can use to help guide students in the decision making process for major selection. You will learn and practice three unique techniques designed to better support and engage Exploring and Redeciding students. Participants Will Be Able To: - Learn how one advising office leveraged campus partnerships to create and maintain institutional buy-in for a new initiative. - Understand how collaboration with the Career and Life Design Center led to a stronger referral process, increased communication and outreach for students, and more congruent one-stop services. - Use research to create advising tools, resources, and new techniques that helped build new adviser training models. - Understand how Advisors approached building new appointment structures and the content in each student appointment. - Understand how to track student progress data and use it effectively. - Understand why changing the culture and stigma of being Undecided (Exploring) matters for this generation of college students. - Practice advising resources, and techniques that have been successful over the past three years via storytelling, dreaming and brainstorming.
